name: NC DEQ DWR "SSOs and Bypasses" (Sanitary Sewer Overflows since Jan 2026) ArcGIS layer
operator: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Water Resources
waters_covered: statewide; named receiving water with NC stream index (e.g. "Salem Creek - 13-17-36-15")
access_detail: https://services2.arcgis.com/kCu40SDxsCGcuUWO/arcgis/rest/services/Sanitary_Sewer_Overflows_since_Jan_2026/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=json (public, no key; maxRecordCount 2000). Backs the "Sanitary Sewer Overflow Tracking Map" Experience 4a50b5dc87844bab9930a5906522a779 (web map 20b6faf89710464bb6e009b44fbc63dc, owner DWR_GIS_Team). 571 rows on 2026-11-03 (Jan 50-74 a month). Sample in raw/sso-sample.json.
cannot_fill: whether the operator issued the press release
cadence: Edited as DWR enters reports; median report latency 15.7 hours after start (2026 rows). Layer lastEditDate 2026-10-30 00:50 UTC, newest report 2026-10-30, so entry may lag a few days. Legal deadline: verbal report within 24 hours.
history: 2026-01-01 to date in this layer; Sept 2022 to Dec 2025 in https://services2.arcgis.com/kCu40SDxsCGcuUWO/arcgis/rest/services/Sanitary_Sewer_Overflows_September_2022_through_December_2025/FeatureServer/0 (3,208 rows).
license: Item description: "The North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality shall not be held liable for any errors in this metadata ... These data cannot be construed to be a legal document." No licence restriction stated.
legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C; permit conditions (24-hour verbal report, 5-day CS-SSO form)
status_reason: Statewide, machine-readable, event-precision SSO feed with start, end, volume, volume to water, receiving water (with DWR stream index), coordinates and 5-day follow-up fields. Built: pipeline/ingest/nc_dwr_sso.py (571 records on 2026-11-04).
notes: Only SSOs reportable to DWR appear (1,000 gallons or more to ground, or any amount reaching surface water): 516 of 571 rows say reached water. deq_program is "Sanitary Sewer Overflow" for every row although the description says storm-related bypasses are included. Not a press release record: it does not say whether the operator issued the 24-hour press release. Timezone settled 2026-11-04: epoch values are true UTC (Raleigh's 2026-05-12 overflow starts 12:21 UTC, the 8:21 a.m. EDT start Raleigh Water published). The ingester also reads any later Sanitary_Sewer_Overflows_since_Jan_<year> layer it finds. | 2026-11-06: the layer has answered 400 "Item does not exist or is inaccessible" since 2026-11-05 (a name never used answers "Invalid URL", so the service seems to exist but is no longer shared). No public replacement: the organisation's service list has no other sewer overflow layer, an ArcGIS Online search finds only the history layer, the viewer and its web map, and the viewer's web map and DEQ's SSO page still point at this layer. The ingester reports the source as unavailable (ok false, meta.unavailable) and keeps the records it read; it also follows any layer the viewer's web map is pointed at.

name: NC DEQ "Information on Sewer System Overflows" page
status_reason: States the reporting rules and links the tracking map, press-release and public-notice templates, 2014 reporting memo, CS-SSO 5-day form.

name: N.C. Gen. Stat. 143-215.1C(b) Publication of Notice of Discharge of Untreated Wastewater
legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b); 24 hours set by S.L. 2013 (S.B. 729), formerly 48 hours
status_reason: The public-notice duty: press release within 24 hours for 1,000 gallons or more reaching surface waters; newspaper notice for 15,000 gallons or more.
notes: (b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred ... The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State." (b)(2): for 15,000 gallons or more "publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county ... and in each county downstream ... significantly affected", captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE", within 10 days after the Secretary approves the form. Raw: raw/gs-143-215.1C.html

name: N.C. Gen. Stat. 143-215.1C(a) Report to Wastewater System Customers
status_reason: A law-named public channel: municipal or domestic collection and treatment works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day give their users or customers and the Department a yearly performance report, within 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year. Register rows per operator (ids ending -annual-report, made by scripts/add_register_rows.py); no web posting is required.
notes: (a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year." Fetched from ncleg.gov on 2026-11-04 with the project user agent (HTTP 200).

name: 15A NCAC 18A .3400 Coastal Recreational Waters Monitoring, Evaluation and Notification
operator: NC Marine Fisheries Commission (rules); NC DEQ Division of Marine Fisheries (advisories)
status_reason: The coastal advisory rules: pending and full swimming advisories from bacteria results (.3403), and advisories with signs for waters impacted by a wastewater spill and at storm-water discharges (.3404). No set number of hours after a spill.
notes: .3404(b): "A swimming advisory shall be issued by the Division and at least one sign shall be posted at the public access to swimming waters that have been impacted by a wastewater system failure." Sign: "WARNING! WASTEWATER SPILL. SWIMMING IS NOT ADVISED IN THESE WATERS BECAUSE OF THE INCREASED RISK OF ILLNESS." .3404(c): storm drain and pipe signs (the Precautionary status). .3403(d) sign text: "ATTENTION: SWIMMING IN THIS AREA IS NOT RECOMMENDED. BACTERIA TESTING INDICATES LEVELS OF CONTAMINATION THAT MAY BE HAZARDOUS TO YOUR HEALTH. THIS ADVISORY AFFECTS WATERS WITHIN 200' OF THIS SIGN."

Precautionary is the storm-water discharge area advisory of .3404(c).
